name: This Is Fine
blurb: A cartoon dog sipping coffee in a burning room, calmly saying "This is fine"
title: This Is Fine Meme: Meaning, Origin & the Dog in Fire
description: "This is fine" is a cartoon of a dog sitting calmly in a burning room, from KC Green's webcomic Gunshow in January 2013. It means pretending a disaster is OK.
h1: What is the "This is fine" meme?
answer: "This is fine" is a two-panel cartoon of a dog sitting at a table with a drink while the room around him burns, smiling and saying "This is fine." It comes from "On Fire", a strip in the American cartoonist KC Green's webcomic Gunshow, posted in January 2013. People use it to show denial or forced calm when everything is going wrong, and The Atlantic later called it the meme that defined a decade.

body: In the first panel, a cartoon dog in a little hat sits at a table with a mug while flames spread across the ceiling and smoke fills the room. In the second, he smiles and says "This is fine." The meme usually stops there.

In the full six-panel strip, the dog keeps reassuring himself with lines like "That's okay, things are going to be okay" while his own body catches fire and starts to melt. Green has said he was going through a hard time personally when he drew it.

head: Date
Event
rows: KC Green posts Gunshow #648, "On Fire", in early January.
The first two panels spread on Reddit and Imgur, usually without credit, and become a reaction image.
The meme hits the mainstream; Adult Swim announces an animated project in January, and in August Green publishes a follow-up, "This is Not Fine".
The Atlantic calls it "The Meme That Defined a Decade"; in June a This is Fine emote arrives in Fortnite.
The video game This is Fine: Maximum Cope, made with Green and announced in 2024, is released.

ul: Work: "Three deadlines today, the server is down, my boss is on holiday. This is fine."
School: the night before an exam you have not started studying for.
Group chats: replying with just the dog when plans fall apart.
Merch and decor: plush dogs and mugs on office desks, as a self-aware joke about stress.

body: The tone is self-mocking: you are the dog, you know the room is on fire, and you are choosing to stay calm anyway.

It is a classic that never really went away, because there is always a new crisis to apply it to. Green owns the comic and sells official prints, shirts and plush toys; a This is Fine dog plush was even spotted in NASA's mission control during the Perseverance Mars landing in February 2021. Green has said he does not need to be paid every time his art is memed, but he has objected when groups used it in ways he disliked. The dog is called Question Hound.

faq.q: Who drew the "This is fine" dog?
faq.a: The American cartoonist KC Green, in his webcomic Gunshow, in January 2013.
It means pretending everything is OK while things clearly fall apart, used as a joke about denial and stress.
He is called Question Hound, but most people just call him the "This is fine" dog.
